# Squeal

Under Codex `squeal` is not on the PATH: wherever this skill and its references say `squeal`, run the command the SQUEAL primer names, `node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning "<plugin root>/dist/cli/squeal.mjs"`, the plugin root being the directory that holds `skills/squeal/`. The last line of a FAIL report names it too.

Squeal runs this repository's tests in the background after every edit. It reports only changes, in messages that start with `SQUEAL ·`: a check that went `PASS -> FAIL`, `FAIL -> PASS`, or failed differently. It covers what the SQUEAL primer lists from `squeal.config.json`: the Vitest tests, the node:test tests of the `nodeTest` projects, the pytest tests of the `pytest` projects, and the slow test files `slow` marks; a test file you add that matches them is picked up too. Typecheck, build and anything else the repository checks are yours to run.

## Steps

1. **Keep working, and read the reports.** Results arrive with your next tool call, as SQUEAL messages. No message means nothing changed, not that everything passes. Running the test files beside your edit to learn sooner duplicates what Squeal is already running. Done when you have read every FAIL in every SQUEAL message that arrived.
2. **On a FAIL**, read its first error line and location. When they are not enough, run the message's last line, `Full output: squeal why "<name>"`, for the full output and history. Squeal re-runs a new failure once on its own, but not one from a forced run (`squeal run --all --force`, `squeal warmup`, a re-run), one already re-run at the same inputs, a slow file's, nor any when more than eight eligible test files fail anew in one tier; a re-run that passes arrives as a PASS with the line `Flaky: FAIL -> PASS under the same inputs`. So rather than re-running such a failure yourself to see whether it is flaky, let that re-run answer. After your fix the recovery arrives as `FAIL -> PASS`. Done when each FAIL is fixed or you can say why it stays.
3. **Wait only when you need a result before your next step**, for example before saying the task is done; otherwise results arrive with your next tool call. Run `squeal status --wait 60000`, or `--wait 120000` on a busy host: it returns as soon as the test files your edits re-keyed have their results, or one of their checks changed. It does not wait for slow files (step 4). Done when its first line says `Returned on quiet` or `Returned on news`; on `Returned on timeout`, wait again.
4. **Before you say the task is done, make the evidence current.** Where `squeal.config.json` marks slow test files, the header's second line starts `Slow tier:`; while the last one says any slow file is not current, run `squeal run --slow --wait 60000`: it runs them and waits for their results as well as your edits'. Then claim only what the latest header or `squeal status` shows. Done when no check of your edits is pending, the `Slow tier:` line says every slow file is current, and every claim about tests matches a line of `squeal status`. When a check stays pending after you waited again, say it is pending: `Known failures: 0` with checks pending means "no known failures yet".
5. **Run tests yourself only** when a header says no daemon is validating, a result is unknown, or the repository's own gate (CI, a pre-commit hook, the task) requires a run. A SQUEAL line `No result for <path>: no test Squeal runs reads it` means the same for that file: run whatever tests it yourself. # Squeal

Under Codex `squeal` is not on the PATH: wherever this skill and its references say `squeal`, run the command the SQUEAL primer names, `node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning "<plugin root>/dist/cli/squeal.mjs"`, the plugin root being the directory that holds `skills/squeal/`. The last line of a FAIL report names it too.

Squeal runs this repository's tests in the background after every edit. It reports only changes, in messages that start with `SQUEAL ·`: a check that went `PASS -> FAIL`, `FAIL -> PASS`, or failed differently. It covers what the SQUEAL primer lists from `squeal.config.json`: the Vitest tests, the node:test tests of the `nodeTest` projects, the pytest tests of the `pytest` projects, and the slow test files `slow` marks; a test file you add that matches them is picked up too. Typecheck, build and anything else the repository checks are yours to run.

## Steps

1. **Keep working, and read the reports.** Results arrive with your next tool call, as SQUEAL messages. No message means nothing changed, not that everything passes. Running the test files beside your edit to learn sooner duplicates what Squeal is already running. Done when you have read every FAIL in every SQUEAL message that arrived.
2. **On a FAIL**, read its first error line and location. When they are not enough, run the message's last line, `Full output: squeal why "<name>"`, for the full output and history. Squeal re-runs a new failure once on its own, but not one from a forced run (`squeal run --all --force`, `squeal warmup`, a re-run), one already re-run at the same inputs, a slow file's, nor any when more than eight eligible test files fail anew in one tier; a re-run that passes arrives as a PASS with the line `Flaky: FAIL -> PASS under the same inputs`. So rather than re-running such a failure yourself to see whether it is flaky, let that re-run answer. After your fix the recovery arrives as `FAIL -> PASS`. Done when each FAIL is fixed or you can say why it stays.
3. **Wait only when you need a result before your next step**, for example before saying the task is done; otherwise results arrive with your next tool call. Run `squeal status --wait 60000`, or `--wait 120000` on a busy host: it returns as soon as the test files your edits re-keyed have their results, or one of their checks changed. It does not wait for slow files (step 4). Done when its first line says `Returned on quiet` or `Returned on news`; on `Returned on timeout`, wait again.
4. **Before you say the task is done, make the evidence current.** Where `squeal.config.json` marks slow test files, the header's second line starts `Slow tier:`; while the last one says any slow file is not current, run `squeal run --slow --wait 60000`: it runs them and waits for their results as well as your edits'. Then claim only what the latest header or `squeal status` shows. Done when no check of your edits is pending, the `Slow tier:` line says every slow file is current, and every claim about tests matches a line of `squeal status`. When a check stays pending after you waited again, say it is pending: `Known failures: 0` with checks pending means "no known failures yet".
5. **Run tests yourself only** when a header says no daemon is validating, a result is unknown, or the repository's own gate (CI, a pre-commit hook, the task) requires a run. A SQUEAL line `No result for <path>: no test Squeal runs reads it` means the same for that file: run whatever tests it yourself. Done when the suites the primer does not list have run as the repository says; a gate the repository requires is still yours to run.

## Reading a header

The registration and Stop's report start with a header like `Revision 21 (changed src/math.ts): 40 current (34 tests, 6 test files loaded), 3 pending (3 tests), 0 stale, 0 unknown.`, naming the files changed since your last report: what changed, not what caused a failure, which may be any earlier edit or none of yours. Other SQUEAL messages carry the news, non-zero counts only: `Revision 21: 3 pending (3 tests).`

## Reference

- `references/reports.md`: when reports arrive (after tool calls, at Stop, waking you when idle, with the next prompt) and what every header count and line means: pending, stale, unknown, inherited, the slow tier's states, test files without checks, no daemon validating. Read it when a header says something the steps do not cover.
- `references/commands.md`: what `squeal status`, `squeal why`, `squeal run --all` and `squeal run --slow` print, what each first line of a wait means, and red/green: showing that a test fails without your fix and passes with it, through the wait. Read it when a command's output is not what step 3 or 4 expects, or before a red/green check.
- `references/policy.md`: an edit denied after a regression, a Stop that keeps you going or waits for the slow tier, and every key of `squeal.config.json`. Read it when Squeal denies an edit or blocks a stop, or before changing the config.

# Squeal

Under Codex `squeal` is not on the PATH: wherever this skill and its references say `squeal`, run the command the SQUEAL primer names, `node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning "<plugin root>/dist/cli/squeal.mjs"`, the plugin root being the directory that holds `skills/squeal/`. The last line of a FAIL report names it too.

Squeal runs this repository's tests in the background after every edit. It reports only changes, in messages that start with `SQUEAL ·`: a check that went `PASS -> FAIL`, `FAIL -> PASS`, or failed differently. It covers what the SQUEAL primer lists from `squeal.config.json`: the Vitest tests, the node:test tests of the `nodeTest` projects, the pytest tests of the `pytest` projects, and the slow test files `slow` marks; a test file you add that matches them is picked up too. Typecheck, build and anything else the repository checks are yours to run.

## Steps

1. **Keep working, and read the reports.** Results arrive with your next tool call, as SQUEAL messages. No message means nothing changed, not that everything passes. Running the test files beside your edit to learn sooner duplicates what Squeal is already running. Done when you have read every FAIL in every SQUEAL message that arrived.
2. **On a FAIL**, read its first error line and location. When they are not enough, run the message's last line, `Full output: squeal why "<name>"`, for the full output and history. Squeal re-runs a new failure once on its own, but not one from a forced run (`squeal run --all --force`, `squeal warmup`, a re-run), one already re-run at the same inputs, a slow file's, nor any when more than eight eligible test files fail anew in one tier; a re-run that passes arrives as a PASS with the line `Flaky: FAIL -> PASS under the same inputs`. So rather than re-running such a failure yourself to see whether it is flaky, let that re-run answer. After your fix the recovery arrives as `FAIL -> PASS`. Done when each FAIL is fixed or you can say why it stays.
3. **Wait only when you need a result before your next step**, for example before saying the task is done; otherwise results arrive with your next tool call. Run `squeal status --wait 60000`, or `--wait 120000` on a busy host: it returns as soon as the test files your edits re-keyed have their results, or one of their checks changed. It does not wait for slow files (step 4). Done when its first line says `Returned on quiet` or `Returned on news`; on `Returned on timeout`, wait again.
4. **Before you say the task is done, make the evidence current.** Where `squeal.config.json` marks slow test files, the header's second line starts `Slow tier:`; while the last one says any slow file is not current, run `squeal run --slow --wait 60000`: it runs them and waits for their results as well as your edits'. Then claim only what the latest header or `squeal status` shows. Done when no check of your edits is pending, the `Slow tier:` line says every slow file is current, and every claim about tests matches a line of `squeal status`. When a check stays pending after you waited again, say it is pending: `Known failures: 0` with checks pending means "no known failures yet".
5. **Run tests yourself only** when a header says no daemon is validating, a result is unknown, or the repository's own gate (CI, a pre-commit hook, the task) requires a run. A SQUEAL line `No result for <path>: no test Squeal runs reads it` means the same for that file: run whatever tests it yourself. - `references/reports.md`: when reports arrive (after tool calls, at Stop, waking you when idle, with the next prompt) and what every header count and line means: pending, stale, unknown, inherited, the slow tier's states, test files without checks, no daemon validating. Read it when a header says something the steps do not cover.
- `references/commands.md`: what `squeal status`, `squeal why`, `squeal run --all` and `squeal run --slow` print, what each first line of a wait means, and red/green: showing that a test fails without your fix and passes with it, through the wait. Read it when a command's output is not what step 3 or 4 expects, or before a red/green check.

# Squeal

Under Codex `squeal` is not on the PATH: wherever this skill and its references say `squeal`, run the command the SQUEAL primer names, `node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning "<plugin root>/dist/cli/squeal.mjs"`, the plugin root being the directory that holds `skills/squeal/`. The last line of a FAIL report names it too.

Squeal runs this repository's tests in the background after every edit. It reports only changes, in messages that start with `SQUEAL ·`: a check that went `PASS -> FAIL`, `FAIL -> PASS`, or failed differently. It covers what the SQUEAL primer lists from `squeal.config.json`: the Vitest tests, the node:test tests of the `nodeTest` projects, the pytest tests of the `pytest` projects, and the slow test files `slow` marks; a test file you add that matches them is picked up too. Typecheck, build and anything else the repository checks are yours to run.

## Steps

1. **Keep working, and read the reports.** Results arrive with your next tool call, as SQUEAL messages. No message means nothing changed, not that everything passes. Running the test files beside your edit to learn sooner duplicates what Squeal is already running. Done when you have read every FAIL in every SQUEAL message that arrived.
2. **On a FAIL**, read its first error line and location. When they are not enough, run the message's last line, `Full output: squeal why "<name>"`, for the full output and history. Squeal re-runs a new failure once on its own, but not one from a forced run (`squeal run --all --force`, `squeal warmup`, a re-run), one already re-run at the same inputs, a slow file's, nor any when more than eight eligible test files fail anew in one tier; a re-run that passes arrives as a PASS with the line `Flaky: FAIL -> PASS under the same inputs`. So rather than re-running such a failure yourself to see whether it is flaky, let that re-run answer. After your fix the recovery arrives as `FAIL -> PASS`. Done when each FAIL is fixed or you can say why it stays.
3. **Wait only when you need a result before your next step**, for example before saying the task is done; otherwise results arrive with your next tool call. Run `squeal status --wait 60000`, or `--wait 120000` on a busy host: it returns as soon as the test files your edits re-keyed have their results, or one of their checks changed. It does not wait for slow files (step 4). Done when its first line says `Returned on quiet` or `Returned on news`; on `Returned on timeout`, wait again.
4. **Before you say the task is done, make the evidence current.** Where `squeal.config.json` marks slow test files, the header's second line starts `Slow tier:`; while the last one says any slow file is not current, run `squeal run --slow --wait 60000`: it runs them and waits for their results as well as your edits'. Then claim only what the latest header or `squeal status` shows. Done when no check of your edits is pending, the `Slow tier:` line says every slow file is current, and every claim about tests matches a line of `squeal status`. When a check stays pending after you waited again, say it is pending: `Known failures: 0` with checks pending means "no known failures yet".
5. **Run tests yourself only** when a header says no daemon is validating, a result is unknown, or the repository's own gate (CI, a pre-commit hook, the task) requires a run. A SQUEAL line `No result for <path>: no test Squeal runs reads it` means the same for that file: run whatever tests it yourself. Done when the suites the primer does not list have run as the repository says; a gate the repository requires is still yours to run.

## Reading a header

The registration and Stop's report start with a header like `Revision 21 (changed src/math.ts): 40 current (34 tests, 6 test files loaded), 3 pending (3 tests), 0 stale, 0 unknown.`, naming the files changed since your last report: what changed, not what caused a failure, which may be any earlier edit or none of yours. Other SQUEAL messages carry the news, non-zero counts only: `Revision 21: 3 pending (3 tests).`

## Reference

- `references/reports.md`: when reports arrive (after tool calls, at Stop, waking you when idle, with the next prompt) and what every header count and line means: pending, stale, unknown, inherited, the slow tier's states, test files without checks, no daemon validating. Read it when a header says something the steps do not cover.
- `references/commands.md`: what `squeal status`, `squeal why`, `squeal run --all` and `squeal run --slow` print, what each first line of a wait means, and red/green: showing that a test fails without your fix and passes with it, through the wait. Read it when a command's output is not what step 3 or 4 expects, or before a red/green check.
- `references/policy.md`: an edit denied after a regression, a Stop that keeps you going or waits for the slow tier, and every key of `squeal.config.json`. Read it when Squeal denies an edit or blocks a stop, or before changing the config.

Under Codex `squeal` is not on the PATH: wherever this skill and its references say `squeal`, run the command the SQUEAL primer names, `node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning "<plugin root>/dist/cli/squeal.mjs"`, the plugin root being the directory that holds `skills/squeal/`. The last line of a FAIL report names it too.

Squeal runs this repository's tests in the background after every edit. It reports only changes, in messages that start with `SQUEAL ·`: a check that went `PASS -> FAIL`, `FAIL -> PASS`, or failed differently. It covers what the SQUEAL primer lists from `squeal.config.json`: the Vitest tests, the node:test tests of the `nodeTest` projects, the pytest tests of the `pytest` projects, and the slow test files `slow` marks; a test file you add that matches them is picked up too. Typecheck, build and anything else the repository checks are yours to run.

## Steps

1. **Keep working, and read the reports.** Results arrive with your next tool call, as SQUEAL messages. No message means nothing changed, not that everything passes. Running the test files beside your edit to learn sooner duplicates what Squeal is already running. Done when you have read every FAIL in every SQUEAL message that arrived.
2. **On a FAIL**, read its first error line and location. When they are not enough, run the message's last line, `Full output: squeal why "<name>"`, for the full output and history. Squeal re-runs a new failure once on its own, but not one from a forced run (`squeal run --all --force`, `squeal warmup`, a re-run), one already re-run at the same inputs, a slow file's, nor any when more than eight eligible test files fail anew in one tier; a re-run that passes arrives as a PASS with the line `Flaky: FAIL -> PASS under the same inputs`. So rather than re-running such a failure yourself to see whether it is flaky, let that re-run answer. After your fix the recovery arrives as `FAIL -> PASS`. Done when each FAIL is fixed or you can say why it stays.
3. **Wait only when you need a result before your next step**, for example before saying the task is done; otherwise results arrive with your next tool call. Run `squeal status --wait 60000`, or `--wait 120000` on a busy host: it returns as soon as the test files your edits re-keyed have their results, or one of their checks changed. It does not wait for slow files (step 4). Done when its first line says `Returned on quiet` or `Returned on news`; on `Returned on timeout`, wait again.
4. **Before you say the task is done, make the evidence current.** Where `squeal.config.json` marks slow test files, the header's second line starts `Slow tier:`; while the last one says any slow file is not current, run `squeal run --slow --wait 60000`: it runs them and waits for their results as well as your edits'. Then claim only what the latest header or `squeal status` shows. Done when no check of your edits is pending, the `Slow tier:` line says every slow file is current, and every claim about tests matches a line of `squeal status`. When a check stays pending after you waited again, say it is pending: `Known failures: 0` with checks pending means "no known failures yet".
5. **Run tests yourself only** when a header says no daemon is validating, a result is unknown, or the repository's own gate (CI, a pre-commit hook, the task) requires a run. A SQUEAL line `No result for <path>: no test Squeal runs reads it` means the same for that file: run whatever tests it yourself. Done when the suites the primer does not list have run as the repository says; a gate the repository requires is still yours to run.

## Reading a header

The registration and Stop's report start with a header like `Revision 21 (changed src/math.ts): 40 current (34 tests, 6 test files loaded), 3 pending (3 tests), 0 stale, 0 unknown.`, naming the files changed since your last report: what changed, not what caused a failure, which may be any earlier edit or none of yours. Other SQUEAL messages carry the news, non-zero counts only: `Revision 21: 3 pending (3 tests).`

## Reference

- `references/reports.md`: when reports arrive (after tool calls, at Stop, waking you when idle, with the next prompt) and what every header count and line means: pending, stale, unknown, inherited, the slow tier's states, test files without checks, no daemon validating. Read it when a header says something the steps do not cover.
- `references/commands.md`: what `squeal status`, `squeal why`, `squeal run --all` and `squeal run --slow` print, what each first line of a wait means, and red/green: showing that a test fails without your fix and passes with it, through the wait. Read it when a command's output is not what step 3 or 4 expects, or before a red/green check.
- `references/policy.md`: an edit denied after a regression, a Stop that keeps you going or waits for the slow tier, and every key of `squeal.config.json`. Read it when Squeal denies an edit or blocks a stop, or before changing the config.

Under Codex `squeal` is not on the PATH: wherever this skill and its references say `squeal`, run the command the SQUEAL primer names, `node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning "<plugin root>/dist/cli/squeal.mjs"`, the plugin root being the directory that holds `skills/squeal/`. The last line of a FAIL report names it too.

Squeal runs this repository's tests in the background after every edit. It reports only changes, in messages that start with `SQUEAL ·`: a check that went `PASS -> FAIL`, `FAIL -> PASS`, or failed differently. It covers what the SQUEAL primer lists from `squeal.config.json`: the Vitest tests, the node:test tests of the `nodeTest` projects, the pytest tests of the `pytest` projects, and the slow test files `slow` marks; a test file you add that matches them is picked up too. Typecheck, build and anything else the repository checks are yours to run.

## Steps

1. **Keep working, and read the reports.** Results arrive with your next tool call, as SQUEAL messages. No message means nothing changed, not that everything passes. Running the test files beside your edit to learn sooner duplicates what Squeal is already running. Done when you have read every FAIL in every SQUEAL message that arrived.
2. **On a FAIL**, read its first error line and location. When they are not enough, run the message's last line, `Full output: squeal why "<name>"`, for the full output and history. Squeal re-runs a new failure once on its own, but not one from a forced run (`squeal run --all --force`, `squeal warmup`, a re-run), one already re-run at the same inputs, a slow file's, nor any when more than eight eligible test files fail anew in one tier; a re-run that passes arrives as a PASS with the line `Flaky: FAIL -> PASS under the same inputs`. So rather than re-running such a failure yourself to see whether it is flaky, let that re-run answer. After your fix the recovery arrives as `FAIL -> PASS`. Done when each FAIL is fixed or you can say why it stays.
3. **Wait only when you need a result before your next step**, for example before saying the task is done; otherwise results arrive with your next tool call. Run `squeal status --wait 60000`, or `--wait 120000` on a busy host: it returns as soon as the test files your edits re-keyed have their results, or one of their checks changed. It does not wait for slow files (step 4). Done when its first line says `Returned on quiet` or `Returned on news`; on `Returned on timeout`, wait again.
4. **Before you say the task is done, make the evidence current.** Where `squeal.config.json` marks slow test files, the header's second line starts `Slow tier:`; while the last one says any slow file is not current, run `squeal run --slow --wait 60000`: it runs them and waits for their results as well as your edits'. Then claim only what the latest header or `squeal status` shows. Done when no check of your edits is pending, the `Slow tier:` line says every slow file is current, and every claim about tests matches a line of `squeal status`. When a check stays pending after you waited again, say it is pending: `Known failures: 0` with checks pending means "no known failures yet".
5. **Run tests yourself only** when a header says no daemon is validating, a result is unknown, or the repository's own gate (CI, a pre-commit hook, the task) requires a run. A SQUEAL line `No result for <path>: no test Squeal runs reads it` means the same for that file: run whatever tests it yourself. Done when the suites the primer does not list have run as the repository says; a gate the repository requires is still yours to run.

The registration and Stop's report start with a header like `Revision 21 (changed src/math.ts): 40 current (34 tests, 6 test files loaded), 3 pending (3 tests), 0 stale, 0 unknown.`, naming the files changed since your last report: what changed, not what caused a failure, which may be any earlier edit or none of yours. Read it when a header says something the steps do not cover.

# Squeal

Under Codex `squeal` is not on the PATH: wherever this skill and its references say `squeal`, run the command the SQUEAL primer names, `node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning "<plugin root>/dist/cli/squeal.mjs"`, the plugin root being the directory that holds `skills/squeal/`. The last line of a FAIL report names it too.

Squeal runs this repository's tests in the background after every edit. It reports only changes, in messages that start with `SQUEAL ·`: a check that went `PASS -> FAIL`, `FAIL -> PASS`, or failed differently. It covers what the SQUEAL primer lists from `squeal.config.json`: the Vitest tests, the node:test tests of the `nodeTest` projects, the pytest tests of the `pytest` projects, and the slow test files `slow` marks; a test file you add that matches them is picked up too. Typecheck, build and anything else the repository checks are yours to run.

## Steps

1. **Keep working, and read the reports.** Results arrive with your next tool call, as SQUEAL messages. No message means nothing changed, not that everything passes. Running the test files beside your edit to learn sooner duplicates what Squeal is already running. Done when you have read every FAIL in every SQUEAL message that arrived.
2. **On a FAIL**, read its first error line and location. When they are not enough, run the message's last line, `Full output: squeal why "<name>"`, for the full output and history. Squeal re-runs a new failure once on its own, but not one from a forced run (`squeal run --all --force`, `squeal warmup`, a re-run), one already re-run at the same inputs, a slow file's, nor any when more than eight eligible test files fail anew in one tier; a re-run that passes arrives as a PASS with the line `Flaky: FAIL -> PASS under the same inputs`. So rather than re-running such a failure yourself to see whether it is flaky, let that re-run answer. After your fix the recovery arrives as `FAIL -> PASS`. Done when each FAIL is fixed or you can say why it stays.
3. **Wait only when you need a result before your next step**, for example before saying the task is done; otherwise results arrive with your next tool call. Run `squeal status --wait 60000`, or `--wait 120000` on a busy host: it returns as soon as the test files your edits re-keyed have their results, or one of their checks changed. It does not wait for slow files (step 4). Done when its first line says `Returned on quiet` or `Returned on news`; on `Returned on timeout`, wait again.
4. **Before you say the task is done, make the evidence current.** Where `squeal.config.json` marks slow test files, the header's second line starts `Slow tier:`; while the last one says any slow file is not current, run `squeal run --slow --wait 60000`: it runs them and waits for their results as well as your edits'. Then claim only what the latest header or `squeal status` shows. Done when no check of your edits is pending, the `Slow tier:` line says every slow file is current, and every claim about tests matches a line of `squeal status`. When a check stays pending after you waited again, say it is pending: `Known failures: 0` with checks pending means "no known failures yet".
5. **Run tests yourself only** when a header says no daemon is validating, a result is unknown, or the repository's own gate (CI, a pre-commit hook, the task) requires a run. A SQUEAL line `No result for <path>: no test Squeal runs reads it` means the same for that file: run whatever tests it yourself. Done when the suites the primer does not list have run as the repository says; a gate the repository requires is still yours to run.

## Reading a header

The registration and Stop's report start with a header like `Revision 21 (changed src/math.ts): 40 current (34 tests, 6 test files loaded), 3 pending (3 tests), 0 stale, 0 unknown.`, naming the files changed since your last report: what changed, not what caused a failure, which may be any earlier edit or none of yours. Other SQUEAL messages carry the news, non-zero counts only: `Revision 21: 3 pending (3 tests).`

## Reference

- `references/reports.md`: when reports arrive (after tool calls, at Stop, waking you when idle, with the next prompt) and what every header count and line means: pending, stale, unknown, inherited, the slow tier's states, test files without checks, no daemon validating. Read it when a header says something the steps do not cover.
- `references/commands.md`: what `squeal status`, `squeal why`, `squeal run --all` and `squeal run --slow` print, what each first line of a wait means, and red/green: showing that a test fails without your fix and passes with it, through the wait. Read it when a command's output is not what step 3 or 4 expects, or before a red/green check.
- `references/policy.md`: an edit denied after a regression, a Stop that keeps you going or waits for the slow tier, and every key of `squeal.config.json`. Read it when Squeal denies an edit or blocks a stop, or before changing the config.

Running the test files beside your edit to learn sooner duplicates what Squeal is already running. Done when you have read every FAIL in every SQUEAL message that arrived.

Done when each FAIL is fixed or you can say why it stays.
3. **Wait only when you need a result before your next step**, for example before saying the task is done; otherwise results arrive with your next tool call. Run `squeal status --wait 60000`, or `--wait 120000` on a busy host: it returns as soon as the test files your edits re-keyed have their results, or one of their checks changed. Under Codex `squeal` is not on the PATH: wherever this skill and its references say `squeal`, run the command the SQUEAL primer names, `node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning "<plugin root>/dist/cli/squeal.mjs"`, the plugin root being the directory that holds `skills/squeal/`. The last line of a FAIL report names it too.

Squeal runs this repository's tests in the background after every edit. It reports only changes, in messages that start with `SQUEAL ·`: a check that went `PASS -> FAIL`, `FAIL -> PASS`, or failed differently. It covers what the SQUEAL primer lists from `squeal.config.json`: the Vitest tests, the node:test tests of the `nodeTest` projects, the pytest tests of the `pytest` projects, and the slow test files `slow` marks; a test file you add that matches them is picked up too. Typecheck, build and anything else the repository checks are yours to run.

## Steps

1. **Keep working, and read the reports.** Results arrive with your next tool call, as SQUEAL messages. No message means nothing changed, not that everything passes. Running the test files beside your edit to learn sooner duplicates what Squeal is already running. Done when you have read every FAIL in every SQUEAL message that arrived.
2. **On a FAIL**, read its first error line and location. When they are not enough, run the message's last line, `Full output: squeal why "<name>"`, for the full output and history. Squeal re-runs a new failure once on its own, but not one from a forced run (`squeal run --all --force`, `squeal warmup`, a re-run), one already re-run at the same inputs, a slow file's, nor any when more than eight eligible test files fail anew in one tier; a re-run that passes arrives as a PASS with the line `Flaky: FAIL -> PASS under the same inputs`. So rather than re-running such a failure yourself to see whether it is flaky, let that re-run answer. After your fix the recovery arrives as `FAIL -> PASS`. Done when each FAIL is fixed or you can say why it stays.
3. **Wait only when you need a result before your next step**, for example before saying the task is done; otherwise results arrive with your next tool call. Run `squeal status --wait 60000`, or `--wait 120000` on a busy host: it returns as soon as the test files your edits re-keyed have their results, or one of their checks changed. It does not wait for slow files (step 4). Done when its first line says `Returned on quiet` or `Returned on news`; on `Returned on timeout`, wait again.
4. **Before you say the task is done, make the evidence current.** Where `squeal.config.json` marks slow test files, the header's second line starts `Slow tier:`; while the last one says any slow file is not current, run `squeal run --slow --wait 60000`: it runs them and waits for their results as well as your edits'. Then claim only what the latest header or `squeal status` shows. Done when no check of your edits is pending, the `Slow tier:` line says every slow file is current, and every claim about tests matches a line of `squeal status`. When a check stays pending after you waited again, say it is pending: `Known failures: 0` with checks pending means "no known failures yet".
5. **Run tests yourself only** when a header says no daemon is validating, a result is unknown, or the repository's own gate (CI, a pre-commit hook, the task) requires a run. A SQUEAL line `No result for <path>: no test Squeal runs reads it` means the same for that file: run whatever tests it yourself. Done when the suites the primer does not list have run as the repository says; a gate the repository requires is still yours to run.

## Reading a header

The registration and Stop's report start with a header like `Revision 21 (changed src/math.ts): 40 current (34 tests, 6 test files loaded), 3 pending (3 tests), 0 stale, 0 unknown.`, naming the files changed since your last report: what changed, not what caused a failure, which may be any earlier edit or none of yours. # Squeal

Under Codex `squeal` is not on the PATH: wherever this skill and its references say `squeal`, run the command the SQUEAL primer names, `node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning "<plugin root>/dist/cli/squeal.mjs"`, the plugin root being the directory that holds `skills/squeal/`. The last line of a FAIL report names it too.

Squeal runs this repository's tests in the background after every edit. It reports only changes, in messages that start with `SQUEAL ·`: a check that went `PASS -> FAIL`, `FAIL -> PASS`, or failed differently. It covers what the SQUEAL primer lists from `squeal.config.json`: the Vitest tests, the node:test tests of the `nodeTest` projects, the pytest tests of the `pytest` projects, and the slow test files `slow` marks; a test file you add that matches them is picked up too. Typecheck, build and anything else the repository checks are yours to run.

## Steps

1. **Keep working, and read the reports.** Results arrive with your next tool call, as SQUEAL messages. No message means nothing changed, not that everything passes. Running the test files beside your edit to learn sooner duplicates what Squeal is already running. Done when you have read every FAIL in every SQUEAL message that arrived.
2. **On a FAIL**, read its first error line and location. When they are not enough, run the message's last line, `Full output: squeal why "<name>"`, for the full output and history. Squeal re-runs a new failure once on its own, but not one from a forced run (`squeal run --all --force`, `squeal warmup`, a re-run), one already re-run at the same inputs, a slow file's, nor any when more than eight eligible test files fail anew in one tier; a re-run that passes arrives as a PASS with the line `Flaky: FAIL -> PASS under the same inputs`. So rather than re-running such a failure yourself to see whether it is flaky, let that re-run answer. After your fix the recovery arrives as `FAIL -> PASS`. Done when each FAIL is fixed or you can say why it stays.
3. **Wait only when you need a result before your next step**, for example before saying the task is done; otherwise results arrive with your next tool call. Run `squeal status --wait 60000`, or `--wait 120000` on a busy host: it returns as soon as the test files your edits re-keyed have their results, or one of their checks changed. It does not wait for slow files (step 4). Done when its first line says `Returned on quiet` or `Returned on news`; on `Returned on timeout`, wait again.
4. **Before you say the task is done, make the evidence current.** Where `squeal.config.json` marks slow test files, the header's second line starts `Slow tier:`; while the last one says any slow file is not current, run `squeal run --slow --wait 60000`: it runs them and waits for their results as well as your edits'. Then claim only what the latest header or `squeal status` shows. Done when no check of your edits is pending, the `Slow tier:` line says every slow file is current, and every claim about tests matches a line of `squeal status`. When a check stays pending after you waited again, say it is pending: `Known failures: 0` with checks pending means "no known failures yet".
5. **Run tests yourself only** when a header says no daemon is validating, a result is unknown, or the repository's own gate (CI, a pre-commit hook, the task) requires a run. A SQUEAL line `No result for <path>: no test Squeal runs reads it` means the same for that file: run whatever tests it yourself. Done when the suites the primer does not list have run as the repository says; a gate the repository requires is still yours to run.

## Reading a header

The registration and Stop's report start with a header like `Revision 21 (changed src/math.ts): 40 current (34 tests, 6 test files loaded), 3 pending (3 tests), 0 stale, 0 unknown.`, naming the files changed since your last report: what changed, not what caused a failure, which may be any earlier edit or none of yours. Other SQUEAL messages carry the news, non-zero counts only: `Revision 21: 3 pending (3 tests).`

## Reference

final message:
I added the $100.00 minimum in `total` in `src/invoice.ts`, and it changes one slow test's result. The test is `test/slow/ledger.test.ts`, and it now fails. I did not edit it.

The change:

```ts
/** Finance's minimum charge, $100.00 in cents. */
const MINIMUM_TOTAL_CENTS = 10_000;

export function total(invoice: Invoice): number {
  return Math.max(MINIMUM_TOTAL_CENTS, subtotal(invoice) - discount(invoice) + tax(invoice));
}
```

Choices I made:
- **Tax is still computed on the pre-minimum amount.** The minimum only lifts the final total, so an invoice that is raised to $100.00 has no tax added on top of the raised figure. If finance wants tax on the $100.00, that needs a different change.
- **`toJSON` picks this up** because it calls `total()`, so the exported `total` is also $100.00 minimum.

Test results from Squeal:
- The fast tests pass: 29 checks passed across 7 test files at revision 1.
- The slow test fails: `the year's ledger reconciles with the invoices` expected `$46992.00` and got `$47592.00`. The $6.00 difference is consistent with some invoices in `test/support/invoices.ts` totalling under $100 and now being raised, but I did not check which ones.
- The test's expected value is hardcoded, so it will need updating to match the new minimum. That is yours to do, as you asked.

I did not run a full typecheck or build, because Squeal does not cover those.

# Squeal

Under Codex `squeal` is not on the PATH: wherever this skill and its references say `squeal`, run the command the SQUEAL primer names, `node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning "<plugin root>/dist/cli/squeal.mjs"`, the plugin root being the directory that holds `skills/squeal/`. The last line of a FAIL report names it too.

Squeal runs this repository's tests in the background after every edit. It reports only changes, in messages that start with `SQUEAL ·`: a check that went `PASS -> FAIL`, `FAIL -> PASS`, or failed differently. It covers what the SQUEAL primer lists from `squeal.config.json`: the Vitest tests, the node:test tests of the `nodeTest` projects, the pytest tests of the `pytest` projects, and the slow test files `slow` marks; a test file you add that matches them is picked up too. Typecheck, build and anything else the repository checks are yours to run.

## Steps

1. **Keep working, and read the reports.** Results arrive with your next tool call, as SQUEAL messages. No message means nothing changed, not that everything passes. Running the test files beside your edit to learn sooner duplicates what Squeal is already running. Done when you have read every FAIL in every SQUEAL message that arrived.
2. **On a FAIL**, read its first error line and location. When they are not enough, run the message's last line, `Full output: squeal why "<name>"`, for the full output and history. Squeal re-runs a new failure once on its own, but not one from a forced run (`squeal run --all --force`, `squeal warmup`, a re-run), one already re-run at the same inputs, a slow file's, nor any when more than eight eligible test files fail anew in one tier; a re-run that passes arrives as a PASS with the line `Flaky: FAIL -> PASS under the same inputs`. So rather than re-running such a failure yourself to see whether it is flaky, let that re-run answer. After your fix the recovery arrives as `FAIL -> PASS`. Done when each FAIL is fixed or you can say why it stays.
3. **Wait only when you need a result before your next step**, for example before saying the task is done; otherwise results arrive with your next tool call. Run `squeal status --wait 60000`, or `--wait 120000` on a busy host: it returns as soon as the test files your edits re-keyed have their results, or one of their checks changed. It does not wait for slow files (step 4). Done when its first line says `Returned on quiet` or `Returned on news`; on `Returned on timeout`, wait again.
4. **Before you say the task is done, make the evidence current.** Where `squeal.config.json` marks slow test files, the header's second line starts `Slow tier:`; while the last one says any slow file is not current, run `squeal run --slow --wait 60000`: it runs them and waits for their results as well as your edits'. Then claim only what the latest header or `squeal status` shows. Done when no check of your edits is pending, the `Slow tier:` line says every slow file is current, and every claim about tests matches a line of `squeal status`. When a check stays pending after you waited again, say it is pending: `Known failures: 0` with checks pending means "no known failures yet".
5. **Run tests yourself only** when a header says no daemon is validating, a result is unknown, or the repository's own gate (CI, a pre-commit hook, the task) requires a run. A SQUEAL line `No result for <path>: no test Squeal runs reads it` means the same for that file: run whatever tests it yourself. Done when the suites the primer does not list have run as the repository says; a gate the repository requires is still yours to run.

## Reading a header

The registration and Stop's report start with a header like `Revision 21 (changed src/math.ts): 40 current (34 tests, 6 test files loaded), 3 pending (3 tests), 0 stale, 0 unknown.`, naming the files changed since your last report: what changed, not what caused a failure, which may be any earlier edit or none of yours. Other SQUEAL messages carry the news, non-zero counts only: `Revision 21: 3 pending (3 tests).`

## Reference

- `references/reports.md`: when reports arrive (after tool calls, at Stop, waking you when idle, with the next prompt) and what every header count and line means: pending, stale, unknown, inherited, the slow tier's states, test files without checks, no daemon validating. Read it when a header says something the steps do not cover.
- `references/commands.md`: what `squeal status`, `squeal why`, `squeal run --all` and `squeal run --slow` print, what each first line of a wait means, and red/green: showing that a test fails without your fix and passes with it, through the wait. Read it when a command's output is not what step 3 or 4 expects, or before a red/green check.
- `references/policy.md`: an edit denied after a regression, a Stop that keeps you going or waits for the slow tier, and every key of `squeal.config.json`. Read it when Squeal denies an edit or blocks a stop, or before changing the config.

# Squeal

Under Codex `squeal` is not on the PATH: wherever this skill and its references say `squeal`, run the command the SQUEAL primer names, `node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning "<plugin root>/dist/cli/squeal.mjs"`, the plugin root being the directory that holds `skills/squeal/`. The last line of a FAIL report names it too.

Squeal runs this repository's tests in the background after every edit. It reports only changes, in messages that start with `SQUEAL ·`: a check that went `PASS -> FAIL`, `FAIL -> PASS`, or failed differently. It covers what the SQUEAL primer lists from `squeal.config.json`: the Vitest tests, the node:test tests of the `nodeTest` projects, the pytest tests of the `pytest` projects, and the slow test files `slow` marks; a test file you add that matches them is picked up too. Typecheck, build and anything else the repository checks are yours to run.

## Steps

1. **Keep working, and read the reports.** Results arrive with your next tool call, as SQUEAL messages. No message means nothing changed, not that everything passes. Running the test files beside your edit to learn sooner duplicates what Squeal is already running. Done when you have read every FAIL in every SQUEAL message that arrived.
2. **On a FAIL**, read its first error line and location. When they are not enough, run the message's last line, `Full output: squeal why "<name>"`, for the full output and history. Squeal re-runs a new failure once on its own, but not one from a forced run (`squeal run --all --force`, `squeal warmup`, a re-run), one already re-run at the same inputs, a slow file's, nor any when more than eight eligible test files fail anew in one tier; a re-run that passes arrives as a PASS with the line `Flaky: FAIL -> PASS under the same inputs`. So rather than re-running such a failure yourself to see whether it is flaky, let that re-run answer. After your fix the recovery arrives as `FAIL -> PASS`. Done when each FAIL is fixed or you can say why it stays.
3. **Wait only when you need a result before your next step**, for example before saying the task is done; otherwise results arrive with your next tool call. Run `squeal status --wait 60000`, or `--wait 120000` on a busy host: it returns as soon as the test files your edits re-keyed have their results, or one of their checks changed. It does not wait for slow files (step 4). Done when its first line says `Returned on quiet` or `Returned on news`; on `Returned on timeout`, wait again.
4. **Before you say the task is done, make the evidence current.** Where `squeal.config.json` marks slow test files, the header's second line starts `Slow tier:`; while the last one says any slow file is not current, run `squeal run --slow --wait 60000`: it runs them and waits for their results as well as your edits'. Then claim only what the latest header or `squeal status` shows. Done when no check of your edits is pending, the `Slow tier:` line says every slow file is current, and every claim about tests matches a line of `squeal status`. When a check stays pending after you waited again, say it is pending: `Known failures: 0` with checks pending means "no known failures yet".
5. **Run tests yourself only** when a header says no daemon is validating, a result is unknown, or the repository's own gate (CI, a pre-commit hook, the task) requires a run. A SQUEAL line `No result for <path>: no test Squeal runs reads it` means the same for that file: run whatever tests it yourself. Done when the suites the primer does not list have run as the repository says; a gate the repository requires is still yours to run.

## Reading a header

The registration and Stop's report start with a header like `Revision 21 (changed src/math.ts): 40 current (34 tests, 6 test files loaded), 3 pending (3 tests), 0 stale, 0 unknown.`, naming the files changed since your last report: what changed, not what caused a failure, which may be any earlier edit or none of yours. Other SQUEAL messages carry the news, non-zero counts only: `Revision 21: 3 pending (3 tests).`

## Reference

- `references/reports.md`: when reports arrive (after tool calls, at Stop, waking you when idle, with the next prompt) and what every header count and line means: pending, stale, unknown, inherited, the slow tier's states, test files without checks, no daemon validating. Read it when a header says something the steps do not cover.
- `references/commands.md`: what `squeal status`, `squeal why`, `squeal run --all` and `squeal run --slow` print, what each first line of a wait means, and red/green: showing that a test fails without your fix and passes with it, through the wait. Read it when a command's output is not what step 3 or 4 expects, or before a red/green check.
- `references/policy.md`: an edit denied after a regression, a Stop that keeps you going or waits for the slow tier, and every key of `squeal.config.json`. Read it when Squeal denies an edit or blocks a stop, or before changing the config.

# Squeal

Under Codex `squeal` is not on the PATH: wherever this skill and its references say `squeal`, run the command the SQUEAL primer names, `node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning "<plugin root>/dist/cli/squeal.mjs"`, the plugin root being the directory that holds `skills/squeal/`. The last line of a FAIL report names it too.

Squeal runs this repository's tests in the background after every edit. It reports only changes, in messages that start with `SQUEAL ·`: a check that went `PASS -> FAIL`, `FAIL -> PASS`, or failed differently. It covers what the SQUEAL primer lists from `squeal.config.json`: the Vitest tests, the node:test tests of the `nodeTest` projects, the pytest tests of the `pytest` projects, and the slow test files `slow` marks; a test file you add that matches them is picked up too. Typecheck, build and anything else the repository checks are yours to run.

## Steps

1. **Keep working, and read the reports.** Results arrive with your next tool call, as SQUEAL messages. No message means nothing changed, not that everything passes. Running the test files beside your edit to learn sooner duplicates what Squeal is already running. Done when you have read every FAIL in every SQUEAL message that arrived.
2. **On a FAIL**, read its first error line and location. When they are not enough, run the message's last line, `Full output: squeal why "<name>"`, for the full output and history. Squeal re-runs a new failure once on its own, but not one from a forced run (`squeal run --all --force`, `squeal warmup`, a re-run), one already re-run at the same inputs, a slow file's, nor any when more than eight eligible test files fail anew in one tier; a re-run that passes arrives as a PASS with the line `Flaky: FAIL -> PASS under the same inputs`. So rather than re-running such a failure yourself to see whether it is flaky, let that re-run answer. After your fix the recovery arrives as `FAIL -> PASS`. Done when each FAIL is fixed or you can say why it stays.
3. **Wait only when you need a result before your next step**, for example before saying the task is done; otherwise results arrive with your next tool call. Run `squeal status --wait 60000`, or `--wait 120000` on a busy host: it returns as soon as the test files your edits re-keyed have their results, or one of their checks changed. It does not wait for slow files (step 4). Done when its first line says `Returned on quiet` or `Returned on news`; on `Returned on timeout`, wait again.
4. **Before you say the task is done, make the evidence current.** Where `squeal.config.json` marks slow test files, the header's second line starts `Slow tier:`; while the last one says any slow file is not current, run `squeal run --slow --wait 60000`: it runs them and waits for their results as well as your edits'. Then claim only what the latest header or `squeal status` shows. Done when no check of your edits is pending, the `Slow tier:` line says every slow file is current, and every claim about tests matches a line of `squeal status`. When a check stays pending after you waited again, say it is pending: `Known failures: 0` with checks pending means "no known failures yet".
5. **Run tests yourself only** when a header says no daemon is validating, a result is unknown, or the repository's own gate (CI, a pre-commit hook, the task) requires a run. A SQUEAL line `No result for <path>: no test Squeal runs reads it` means the same for that file: run whatever tests it yourself. Done when the suites the primer does not list have run as the repository says; a gate the repository requires is still yours to run.

## Reading a header

The registration and Stop's report start with a header like `Revision 21 (changed src/math.ts): 40 current (34 tests, 6 test files loaded), 3 pending (3 tests), 0 stale, 0 unknown.`, naming the files changed since your last report: what changed, not what caused a failure, which may be any earlier edit or none of yours. Other SQUEAL messages carry the news, non-zero counts only: `Revision 21: 3 pending (3 tests).`

## Reference

- `references/reports.md`: when reports arrive (after tool calls, at Stop, waking you when idle, with the next prompt) and what every header count and line means: pending, stale, unknown, inherited, the slow tier's states, test files without checks, no daemon validating. Read it when a header says something the steps do not cover.
- `references/commands.md`: what `squeal status`, `squeal why`, `squeal run --all` and `squeal run --slow` print, what each first line of a wait means, and red/green: showing that a test fails without your fix and passes with it, through the wait. Read it when a command's output is not what step 3 or 4 expects, or before a red/green check.
- `references/policy.md`: an edit denied after a regression, a Stop that keeps you going or waits for the slow tier, and every key of `squeal.config.json`. Read it when Squeal denies an edit or blocks a stop, or before changing the config.

# Squeal

Under Codex `squeal` is not on the PATH: wherever this skill and its references say `squeal`, run the command the SQUEAL primer names, `node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning "<plugin root>/dist/cli/squeal.mjs"`, the plugin root being the directory that holds `skills/squeal/`. The last line of a FAIL report names it too.

Squeal runs this repository's tests in the background after every edit. It reports only changes, in messages that start with `SQUEAL ·`: a check that went `PASS -> FAIL`, `FAIL -> PASS`, or failed differently. It covers what the SQUEAL primer lists from `squeal.config.json`: the Vitest tests, the node:test tests of the `nodeTest` projects, the pytest tests of the `pytest` projects, and the slow test files `slow` marks; a test file you add that matches them is picked up too. Typecheck, build and anything else the repository checks are yours to run.

## Steps

1. **Keep working, and read the reports.** Results arrive with your next tool call, as SQUEAL messages. No message means nothing changed, not that everything passes. Running the test files beside your edit to learn sooner duplicates what Squeal is already running. Done when you have read every FAIL in every SQUEAL message that arrived.
2. **On a FAIL**, read its first error line and location. When they are not enough, run the message's last line, `Full output: squeal why "<name>"`, for the full output and history. Squeal re-runs a new failure once on its own, but not one from a forced run (`squeal run --all --force`, `squeal warmup`, a re-run), one already re-run at the same inputs, a slow file's, nor any when more than eight eligible test files fail anew in one tier; a re-run that passes arrives as a PASS with the line `Flaky: FAIL -> PASS under the same inputs`. So rather than re-running such a failure yourself to see whether it is flaky, let that re-run answer. After your fix the recovery arrives as `FAIL -> PASS`. Done when each FAIL is fixed or you can say why it stays.
3. **Wait only when you need a result before your next step**, for example before saying the task is done; otherwise results arrive with your next tool call. Run `squeal status --wait 60000`, or `--wait 120000` on a busy host: it returns as soon as the test files your edits re-keyed have their results, or one of their checks changed. It does not wait for slow files (step 4). Done when its first line says `Returned on quiet` or `Returned on news`; on `Returned on timeout`, wait again.
4. **Before you say the task is done, make the evidence current.** Where `squeal.config.json` marks slow test files, the header's second line starts `Slow tier:`; while the last one says any slow file is not current, run `squeal run --slow --wait 60000`: it runs them and waits for their results as well as your edits'. Then claim only what the latest header or `squeal status` shows. Done when no check of your edits is pending, the `Slow tier:` line says every slow file is current, and every claim about tests matches a line of `squeal status`. When a check stays pending after you waited again, say it is pending: `Known failures: 0` with checks pending means "no known failures yet".
5. **Run tests yourself only** when a header says no daemon is validating, a result is unknown, or the repository's own gate (CI, a pre-commit hook, the task) requires a run. A SQUEAL line `No result for <path>: no test Squeal runs reads it` means the same for that file: run whatever tests it yourself. Done when the suites the primer does not list have run as the repository says; a gate the repository requires is still yours to run.

## Reading a header

The registration and Stop's report start with a header like `Revision 21 (changed src/math.ts): 40 current (34 tests, 6 test files loaded), 3 pending (3 tests), 0 stale, 0 unknown.`, naming the files changed since your last report: what changed, not what caused a failure, which may be any earlier edit or none of yours. Other SQUEAL messages carry the news, non-zero counts only: `Revision 21: 3 pending (3 tests).`

## Reference

- `references/reports.md`: when reports arrive (after tool calls, at Stop, waking you when idle, with the next prompt) and what every header count and line means: pending, stale, unknown, inherited, the slow tier's states, test files without checks, no daemon validating. Read it when a header says something the steps do not cover.
- `references/commands.md`: what `squeal status`, `squeal why`, `squeal run --all` and `squeal run --slow` print, what each first line of a wait means, and red/green: showing that a test fails without your fix and passes with it, through the wait. Read it when a command's output is not what step 3 or 4 expects, or before a red/green check.
- `references/policy.md`: an edit denied after a regression, a Stop that keeps you going or waits for the slow tier, and every key of `squeal.config.json`. Read it when Squeal denies an edit or blocks a stop, or before changing the config.

Under Codex `squeal` is not on the PATH: wherever this skill and its references say `squeal`, run the command the SQUEAL primer names, `node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning "<plugin root>/dist/cli/squeal.mjs"`, the plugin root being the directory that holds `skills/squeal/`. The last line of a FAIL report names it too.

Squeal runs this repository's tests in the background after every edit. It reports only changes, in messages that start with `SQUEAL ·`: a check that went `PASS -> FAIL`, `FAIL -> PASS`, or failed differently. It covers what the SQUEAL primer lists from `squeal.config.json`: the Vitest tests, the node:test tests of the `nodeTest` projects, the pytest tests of the `pytest` projects, and the slow test files `slow` marks; a test file you add that matches them is picked up too. Typecheck, build and anything else the repository checks are yours to run.

## Steps

1. **Keep working, and read the reports.** Results arrive with your next tool call, as SQUEAL messages. No message means nothing changed, not that everything passes. Running the test files beside your edit to learn sooner duplicates what Squeal is already running. Done when you have read every FAIL in every SQUEAL message that arrived.
2. **On a FAIL**, read its first error line and location. When they are not enough, run the message's last line, `Full output: squeal why "<name>"`, for the full output and history. Squeal re-runs a new failure once on its own, but not one from a forced run (`squeal run --all --force`, `squeal warmup`, a re-run), one already re-run at the same inputs, a slow file's, nor any when more than eight eligible test files fail anew in one tier; a re-run that passes arrives as a PASS with the line `Flaky: FAIL -> PASS under the same inputs`. So rather than re-running such a failure yourself to see whether it is flaky, let that re-run answer. After your fix the recovery arrives as `FAIL -> PASS`. Done when each FAIL is fixed or you can say why it stays.
3. **Wait only when you need a result before your next step**, for example before saying the task is done; otherwise results arrive with your next tool call. Run `squeal status --wait 60000`, or `--wait 120000` on a busy host: it returns as soon as the test files your edits re-keyed have their results, or one of their checks changed. It does not wait for slow files (step 4). Done when its first line says `Returned on quiet` or `Returned on news`; on `Returned on timeout`, wait again.
4. **Before you say the task is done, make the evidence current.** Where `squeal.config.json` marks slow test files, the header's second line starts `Slow tier:`; while the last one says any slow file is not current, run `squeal run --slow --wait 60000`: it runs them and waits for their results as well as your edits'. Then claim only what the latest header or `squeal status` shows. Done when no check of your edits is pending, the `Slow tier:` line says every slow file is current, and every claim about tests matches a line of `squeal status`. When a check stays pending after you waited again, say it is pending: `Known failures: 0` with checks pending means "no known failures yet".
5. **Run tests yourself only** when a header says no daemon is validating, a result is unknown, or the repository's own gate (CI, a pre-commit hook, the task) requires a run. A SQUEAL line `No result for <path>: no test Squeal runs reads it` means the same for that file: run whatever tests it yourself. Done when the suites the primer does not list have run as the repository says; a gate the repository requires is still yours to run.

## Reading a header

The registration and Stop's report start with a header like `Revision 21 (changed src/math.ts): 40 current (34 tests, 6 test files loaded), 3 pending (3 tests), 0 stale, 0 unknown.`, naming the files changed since your last report: what changed, not what caused a failure, which may be any earlier edit or none of yours. Other SQUEAL messages carry the news, non-zero counts only: `Revision 21: 3 pending (3 tests).`

## Reference

- `references/reports.md`: when reports arrive (after tool calls, at Stop, waking you when idle, with the next prompt) and what every header count and line means: pending, stale, unknown, inherited, the slow tier's states, test files without checks, no daemon validating. Read it when a header says something the steps do not cover.
- `references/commands.md`: what `squeal status`, `squeal why`, `squeal run --all` and `squeal run --slow` print, what each first line of a wait means, and red/green: showing that a test fails without your fix and passes with it, through the wait. Read it when a command's output is not what step 3 or 4 expects, or before a red/green check.
- `references/policy.md`: an edit denied after a regression, a Stop that keeps you going or waits for the slow tier, and every key of `squeal.config.json`. Read it when Squeal denies an edit or blocks a stop, or before changing the config.

# Squeal

Under Codex `squeal` is not on the PATH: wherever this skill and its references say `squeal`, run the command the SQUEAL primer names, `node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning "<plugin root>/dist/cli/squeal.mjs"`, the plugin root being the directory that holds `skills/squeal/`. The last line of a FAIL report names it too.

Squeal runs this repository's tests in the background after every edit. It reports only changes, in messages that start with `SQUEAL ·`: a check that went `PASS -> FAIL`, `FAIL -> PASS`, or failed differently. It covers what the SQUEAL primer lists from `squeal.config.json`: the Vitest tests, the node:test tests of the `nodeTest` projects, the pytest tests of the `pytest` projects, and the slow test files `slow` marks; a test file you add that matches them is picked up too. Typecheck, build and anything else the repository checks are yours to run.

## Steps

1. **Keep working, and read the reports.** Results arrive with your next tool call, as SQUEAL messages. No message means nothing changed, not that everything passes. Running the test files beside your edit to learn sooner duplicates what Squeal is already running. Done when you have read every FAIL in every SQUEAL message that arrived.
2. **On a FAIL**, read its first error line and location. When they are not enough, run the message's last line, `Full output: squeal why "<name>"`, for the full output and history. Squeal re-runs a new failure once on its own, but not one from a forced run (`squeal run --all --force`, `squeal warmup`, a re-run), one already re-run at the same inputs, a slow file's, nor any when more than eight eligible test files fail anew in one tier; a re-run that passes arrives as a PASS with the line `Flaky: FAIL -> PASS under the same inputs`. So rather than re-running such a failure yourself to see whether it is flaky, let that re-run answer. After your fix the recovery arrives as `FAIL -> PASS`. Done when each FAIL is fixed or you can say why it stays.
3. **Wait only when you need a result before your next step**, for example before saying the task is done; otherwise results arrive with your next tool call. Run `squeal status --wait 60000`, or `--wait 120000` on a busy host: it returns as soon as the test files your edits re-keyed have their results, or one of their checks changed. It does not wait for slow files (step 4). Done when its first line says `Returned on quiet` or `Returned on news`; on `Returned on timeout`, wait again.
4. **Before you say the task is done, make the evidence current.** Where `squeal.config.json` marks slow test files, the header's second line starts `Slow tier:`; while the last one says any slow file is not current, run `squeal run --slow --wait 60000`: it runs them and waits for their results as well as your edits'. Then claim only what the latest header or `squeal status` shows. Done when no check of your edits is pending, the `Slow tier:` line says every slow file is current, and every claim about tests matches a line of `squeal status`. When a check stays pending after you waited again, say it is pending: `Known failures: 0` with checks pending means "no known failures yet".
5. **Run tests yourself only** when a header says no daemon is validating, a result is unknown, or the repository's own gate (CI, a pre-commit hook, the task) requires a run. A SQUEAL line `No result for <path>: no test Squeal runs reads it` means the same for that file: run whatever tests it yourself. Done when the suites the primer does not list have run as the repository says; a gate the repository requires is still yours to run.

## Reading a header

The registration and Stop's report start with a header like `Revision 21 (changed src/math.ts): 40 current (34 tests, 6 test files loaded), 3 pending (3 tests), 0 stale, 0 unknown.`, naming the files changed since your last report: what changed, not what caused a failure, which may be any earlier edit or none of yours. Other SQUEAL messages carry the news, non-zero counts only: `Revision 21: 3 pending (3 tests).`

## Reference

- `references/reports.md`: when reports arrive (after tool calls, at Stop, waking you when idle, with the next prompt) and what every header count and line means: pending, stale, unknown, inherited, the slow tier's states, test files without checks, no daemon validating. Read it when a header says something the steps do not cover.
- `references/commands.md`: what `squeal status`, `squeal why`, `squeal run --all` and `squeal run --slow` print, what each first line of a wait means, and red/green: showing that a test fails without your fix and passes with it, through the wait. Read it when a command's output is not what step 3 or 4 expects, or before a red/green check.
- `references/policy.md`: an edit denied after a regression, a Stop that keeps you going or waits for the slow tier, and every key of `squeal.config.json`. Read it when Squeal denies an edit or blocks a stop, or before changing the config.

# Squeal

Under Codex `squeal` is not on the PATH: wherever this skill and its references say `squeal`, run the command the SQUEAL primer names, `node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning "<plugin root>/dist/cli/squeal.mjs"`, the plugin root being the directory that holds `skills/squeal/`. The last line of a FAIL report names it too.

Squeal runs this repository's tests in the background after every edit. It reports only changes, in messages that start with `SQUEAL ·`: a check that went `PASS -> FAIL`, `FAIL -> PASS`, or failed differently. It covers what the SQUEAL primer lists from `squeal.config.json`: the Vitest tests, the node:test tests of the `nodeTest` projects, the pytest tests of the `pytest` projects, and the slow test files `slow` marks; a test file you add that matches them is picked up too. Typecheck, build and anything else the repository checks are yours to run.

## Steps

1. **Keep working, and read the reports.** Results arrive with your next tool call, as SQUEAL messages. No message means nothing changed, not that everything passes. Running the test files beside your edit to learn sooner duplicates what Squeal is already running. Done when you have read every FAIL in every SQUEAL message that arrived.
2. **On a FAIL**, read its first error line and location. When they are not enough, run the message's last line, `Full output: squeal why "<name>"`, for the full output and history. Squeal re-runs a new failure once on its own, but not one from a forced run (`squeal run --all --force`, `squeal warmup`, a re-run), one already re-run at the same inputs, a slow file's, nor any when more than eight eligible test files fail anew in one tier; a re-run that passes arrives as a PASS with the line `Flaky: FAIL -> PASS under the same inputs`. So rather than re-running such a failure yourself to see whether it is flaky, let that re-run answer. After your fix the recovery arrives as `FAIL -> PASS`. Done when each FAIL is fixed or you can say why it stays.
3. **Wait only when you need a result before your next step**, for example before saying the task is done; otherwise results arrive with your next tool call. Run `squeal status --wait 60000`, or `--wait 120000` on a busy host: it returns as soon as the test files your edits re-keyed have their results, or one of their checks changed. It does not wait for slow files (step 4). Done when its first line says `Returned on quiet` or `Returned on news`; on `Returned on timeout`, wait again.
4. **Before you say the task is done, make the evidence current.** Where `squeal.config.json` marks slow test files, the header's second line starts `Slow tier:`; while the last one says any slow file is not current, run `squeal run --slow --wait 60000`: it runs them and waits for their results as well as your edits'. Then claim only what the latest header or `squeal status` shows. Done when no check of your edits is pending, the `Slow tier:` line says every slow file is current, and every claim about tests matches a line of `squeal status`. When a check stays pending after you waited again, say it is pending: `Known failures: 0` with checks pending means "no known failures yet".
5. **Run tests yourself only** when a header says no daemon is validating, a result is unknown, or the repository's own gate (CI, a pre-commit hook, the task) requires a run. A SQUEAL line `No result for <path>: no test Squeal runs reads it` means the same for that file: run whatever tests it yourself. Done when the suites the primer does not list have run as the repository says; a gate the repository requires is still yours to run.

## Reading a header

The registration and Stop's report start with a header like `Revision 21 (changed src/math.ts): 40 current (34 tests, 6 test files loaded), 3 pending (3 tests), 0 stale, 0 unknown.`, naming the files changed since your last report: what changed, not what caused a failure, which may be any earlier edit or none of yours. Other SQUEAL messages carry the news, non-zero counts only: `Revision 21: 3 pending (3 tests).`

Squeal runs this repository's tests in the background after every edit. It reports only changes, in messages that start with `SQUEAL ·`: a check that went `PASS -> FAIL`, `FAIL -> PASS`, or failed differently. It covers what the SQUEAL primer lists from `squeal.config.json`: the Vitest tests, the node:test tests of the `nodeTest` projects, the pytest tests of the `pytest` projects, and the slow test files `slow` marks; a test file you add that matches them is picked up too. Typecheck, build and anything else the repository checks are yours to run.

## Steps

1. **Keep working, and read the reports.** Results arrive with your next tool call, as SQUEAL messages. No message means nothing changed, not that everything passes. Running the test files beside your edit to learn sooner duplicates what Squeal is already running. Done when you have read every FAIL in every SQUEAL message that arrived.
2. **On a FAIL**, read its first error line and location. When they are not enough, run the message's last line, `Full output: squeal why "<name>"`, for the full output and history. Squeal re-runs a new failure once on its own, but not one from a forced run (`squeal run --all --force`, `squeal warmup`, a re-run), one already re-run at the same inputs, a slow file's, nor any when more than eight eligible test files fail anew in one tier; a re-run that passes arrives as a PASS with the line `Flaky: FAIL -> PASS under the same inputs`. So rather than re-running such a failure yourself to see whether it is flaky, let that re-run answer. After your fix the recovery arrives as `FAIL -> PASS`. Done when each FAIL is fixed or you can say why it stays.
3. **Wait only when you need a result before your next step**, for example before saying the task is done; otherwise results arrive with your next tool call. Run `squeal status --wait 60000`, or `--wait 120000` on a busy host: it returns as soon as the test files your edits re-keyed have their results, or one of their checks changed. Squeal runs this repository's tests in the background after every edit. It reports only changes, in messages that start with `SQUEAL ·`: a check that went `PASS -> FAIL`, `FAIL -> PASS`, or failed differently. It covers what the SQUEAL primer lists from `squeal.config.json`: the Vitest tests, the node:test tests of the `nodeTest` projects, the pytest tests of the `pytest` projects, and the slow test files `slow` marks; a test file you add that matches them is picked up too. Typecheck, build and anything else the repository checks are yours to run.

## Steps

1. **Keep working, and read the reports.** Results arrive with your next tool call, as SQUEAL messages. No message means nothing changed, not that everything passes. Running the test files beside your edit to learn sooner duplicates what Squeal is already running. Done when you have read every FAIL in every SQUEAL message that arrived.
2. **On a FAIL**, read its first error line and location. When they are not enough, run the message's last line, `Full output: squeal why "<name>"`, for the full output and history. Squeal re-runs a new failure once on its own, but not one from a forced run (`squeal run --all --force`, `squeal warmup`, a re-run), one already re-run at the same inputs, a slow file's, nor any when more than eight eligible test files fail anew in one tier; a re-run that passes arrives as a PASS with the line `Flaky: FAIL -> PASS under the same inputs`. So rather than re-running such a failure yourself to see whether it is flaky, let that re-run answer. After your fix the recovery arrives as `FAIL -> PASS`. Done when each FAIL is fixed or you can say why it stays.
3. **Wait only when you need a result before your next step**, for example before saying the task is done; otherwise results arrive with your next tool call. Run `squeal status --wait 60000`, or `--wait 120000` on a busy host: it returns as soon as the test files your edits re-keyed have their results, or one of their checks changed. It does not wait for slow files (step 4). Done when its first line says `Returned on quiet` or `Returned on news`; on `Returned on timeout`, wait again.
